## Load packages

`clusterProfiler` runs the enrichment and `enrichplot` draws it; `enrichVolcano` (not on CRAN) is
called with `::` for its label cleaner.

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, dplyr, purrr, ggplot2, readxl, clusterProfiler, enrichplot)
here::i_am("03_Pathway_Enrichment/07_pathway_maps/a_script/07_pathway_maps.qmd")
```

## Read inputs

Pathway maps of the two training responses: which pathways each leg moves, how they cluster by
shared proteins, and which proteins link them. Figures only; every test stays in
`01_run_fgsea_and_fry`. Adapted from Sam's PR #26 (sc-norton).

```{r read}
stage <- here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "07_pathway_maps")
book <- here(
  "03_Pathway_Enrichment", "01_run_fgsea_and_fry", "c_data", "01_run_fgsea_and_fry.xlsx"
)
protein_results <- read_excel(book, "protein_results")
set_tests <- read_excel(book, "set_tests")
sets <- readRDS(here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "00_build_gene_sets", "c_data", "gene_sets.rds"))
arms <- c(BFR = "BFR_Post-Pre", HLRT = "HLRT_Post-Pre")
```

## Rank the proteins

The ranking of `01`, so the maps draw the same enrichment that was tested.

```{r ranked}
ranked <- map(arms, function(cn) {
  with(filter(protein_results, contrast == cn, selected), sort(set_names(t, gene), TRUE))
})
set_labels <- set_tests |>
  distinct(set_id, database, pathway) |>
  mutate(label = enrichVolcano::clean_label(pathway, width = 1000))
```

## Choose the pathways to draw

The main sets `01` kept, one per cluster of overlapping sets, significant at FDR < 0.05 in either
leg. A collection with more than 30 is cut to the 30 with the smallest adjusted p.

```{r drawn}
drawn <- set_tests |>
  filter(method == "fgsea", contrast %in% arms, padj < 0.05, main) |>
  summarise(padj = min(padj), .by = c(set_id, database)) |>
  slice_min(padj, n = 30, by = database, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  left_join(select(set_labels, set_id, label), by = "set_id")
count(drawn, database)
```

## Run the enrichment

enrichplot's maps need a clusterProfiler result, so `compareCluster()` runs GSEA on both rankings
per collection, with the sets and size limits of `01`. clusterProfiler 4.20 runs GSEA through
enrichit, whose multilevel code derives from fgsea's but is separate, so the NES are checked
against `01` below.

```{r run-gsea}
compared <- map(set_names(unique(set_labels$database)), function(db) {
  set.seed(1)
  # GSEA() drops `...`, so eps never reaches enrichit and p below 1e-10 is floored with a warning.
  # The floored p reach no figure: the pathways come from 01, and colour is NES.
  suppressWarnings(compareCluster(
    ranked,
    fun = "GSEA",
    TERM2GENE = stack(sets[startsWith(names(sets), paste0(db, "|"))])[, c("ind", "values")],
    TERM2NAME = select(filter(set_labels, database == db), set_id, label),
    minGSSize = 15, maxGSSize = 500, pvalueCutoff = 1, verbose = FALSE
  ))
})
```

## Check against 01

NES of this run against `set_tests`, per collection.

```{r check}
nes_check <- compared |>
  map(function(result) {
    transmute(
      as.data.frame(result),
      set_id = as.character(ID), contrast = arms[as.character(Cluster)], NES_07 = NES
    )
  }) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  inner_join(
    filter(set_tests, method == "fgsea") |> select(set_id, database, contrast, NES),
    by = c("set_id", "contrast")
  )
nes_check |>
  summarise(
    pairs = n(), r = cor(NES_07, NES), max_abs_diff = max(abs(NES_07 - NES)), .by = database
  )
```

## Draw figures

Four pages per collection, in one PDF. Pathway similarity is computed only among the drawn
pathways, since GO:BP holds 1,366 sets.

- S19, dotplot: BFR and HLRT side by side, colour NES, dot size the share of the pathway in its
  leading edge.
- S20, enrichment map: a network with pathways as nodes, joined when their proteins overlap, each
  node a pie split by leg.
- S21, tree: pathways clustered by shared proteins, each cluster named by its most frequent words.
- S22, network: the five strongest pathways linked to their leading-edge proteins.

```{r maps}
figure_title <- function(number, title, db) {
  labs(title = sprintf("S%d. %s, %s", number, title, db))
}
arm_fill <- scale_fill_manual(values = c(BFR = "#B2182B", HLRT = "#2166AC"), name = NULL)
collection_order <- c("Hallmark", "GO_Slim", "KEGG_Legacy", "Reactome", "GOBP")
stopifnot(setequal(collection_order, drawn$database))
pdf(file.path(stage, "b_reports", "07_pathway_maps.pdf"), width = 8.27, height = 11.69)
for (db in collection_order) {
  show <- filter(drawn, database == db)$label
  shown <- filter(compared[[db]], Description %in% show)
  similar <- pairwise_termsim(shown, showCategory = length(show))
  pages <- list(
    # dotplot logs its colour scale, built for p-values; NES is signed, so a diverging scale.
    dotplot(shown, showCategory = length(show), color = "NES", label_format = 45) +
      scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", name = "NES") +
      figure_title(19, "Pathways by leg", db),
    # On the two small collections (Hallmark, GO Slim) few pathways share proteins, and emapplot
    # warns from an internal max() over no edges; the map still draws.
    suppressWarnings(
      emapplot(similar, showCategory = length(show), label_format = 30, size_category = 1.6)
    ) + arm_fill + figure_title(20, "Enrichment map", db),
    treeplot(
      similar,
      showCategory = length(show), nCluster = min(5, length(show) - 1), label_format = 32,
      fontsize_tiplab = 2.6, fontsize_cladelab = 2.6, hexpand = 0.5, cladelab_offset = 9
    ) + arm_fill + figure_title(21, "Pathway tree", db),
    cnetplot(shown, showCategory = head(show, 5), node_label = "category") + arm_fill +
      figure_title(22, "Pathways and their proteins", db)
  )
  walk(pages, print)
}
invisible(dev.off())
```

## Summary

How many of the drawn sets each leg calls at FDR < 0.05.

```{r summary}
set_tests |>
  filter(method == "fgsea", contrast %in% arms, set_id %in% drawn$set_id) |>
  summarise(drawn = n(), fdr_05 = sum(padj < 0.05), .by = c(database, contrast))
```
